AgeView.description:
Knowledge-time distance from the snapshot known_at of the run's first publication to
the report's evidence horizon. Not time since publication, not the age of the evidence,
not time open. ``published_run_start`` (definition 1.0.0) crossed unpublished epochs;
``contiguous_fail_run_start`` (1.1.0) stops at them and at a change of engine.
AgeView.title: AgeView

AggregateDisclosureView.description:
A restricted projection of a registered report's summary under a disclosure policy.

A new artifact, not the report: it carries no identifier, hash, date, scope, profile,
engine, filter, segment or case key of the original. ``view_id`` is random and opaque;
it neither authenticates the view nor grants access to it.
AggregateDisclosureView.title: AggregateDisclosureView

BlockKey.description: An engine-recorded block of an UNKNOWN control (the decisive check of its diagnosis).
BlockKey.title: BlockKey

ChainCoverageScope.description:
Which chain records a certificate read: network, ingestion target (asset
and account), route and the ExecutionLinks the run applied (``links_sha256``: they
decide which notes are quarantined and which records list a link). Two certificates can
replace one another only within the same network, target, account, asset and links, and
only towards a route that includes the other's.

``not_covered``: effects of the asset this route cannot see for this target (by role and
route); absence of one of them can never be argued from this certificate. An
empty list declares that nothing is out of sight; absent (None) declares
nothing, and under the scoped-absence rule it is never read as "nothing out of sight".
ChainCoverageScope.title: ChainCoverageScope

ChainEffectPayload.description:
One on-chain effect on the target asset, from one representation.

Classic effects (debit, credit, failed): ``account`` is the base account whose balance
of the target asset Horizon reports as debited or credited by the operation; they
carry the operation context and the transaction outcome. A failed operation keeps its
technical result, never an amount.

SAC legs: ``account``/``counterparty`` are the parties of one CAP-67 event, seen from
its sender (or from its receiver when the sender is not an account). A leg is evidence
of the event, not of an effective balance change of ``account``: conversion legs of a
path payment can pass through accounts whose Classic balance does not change.

DEX fills (``dex_fill``): an offer of the watched account crossed, or the watched
account's own offer operation crossing others. Classic fills come from Horizon trade
effects (executed amounts of both assets, offer id); SAC fills from the CAP-67 event,
seen from the watched account. ``unresolved_movement``: a SAC movement whose origin
could not be established; it is kept, and it satisfies nothing.

Typed parties (increment 3): a SAC movement between an account and a contract
(``contract_transfer``), a liquidity pool (``pool_transfer``) or a claimable balance
(``claimable_balance_created`` into it, ``claimable_balance_claimed`` out of it).
``account`` is the account side (the issuer for a mint or burn), ``counterparty`` the
typed party. A clawback whose holder is not an account names it in ``holder`` and has
no ``account``. None of them is evidence of fulfilment: a technically complete
representation still proves no payment, delivery or redemption.
ChainEffectPayload.title: ChainEffectPayload

ChainParty.description:
A typed technical entity on the ledger.

None of them, an account included, is by itself an economic holder, a beneficiary or a
person: a contract's owner, a claimable balance's eventual recipient and a pool's
liquidity providers are never inferred from the identifier. ``id`` is the native
identifier in its lossless SEP-23 strkey form (G account, C contract, B claimable
balance, L liquidity pool), so a contract, balance or pool never reads as an account.
An ``unresolved`` party is one the evidence does not identify: it has no id and says
why. A party's identity is its kind and id on the network of the effect that names it
(``party_identity``).
ChainParty.title: ChainParty

ChangeView.description:
This publication against the previous publication of the same operation (the one
of highest epoch below it). Stored documents only, except ``blocks`` (diagnosis replay).
ChangeView.title: ChangeView

CitedEvidenceChange.description: Evidence references cited by controls (``evidence_refs``), counted, never listed.
CitedEvidenceChange.title: CitedEvidenceChange

ClaimableBalanceContext.description:
A claimable balance's technical participants, as Horizon
reports its history (``/claimable_balances/{id}/operations``).

``creator`` is the account whose balance was debited when the balance was created (the
issuer when it was minted into it), or ``unresolved``. ``claimants`` may claim it: a
claimant has received nothing until a claim is observed, and none of them is the owner
of the account debited at creation. None means the history could not be read; the
participants are then unknown and the relevance of the effect cannot be ruled out.
``operation_type`` and ``operation_source`` are those of this effect's operation as
Horizon reports them (None when it could not be read).
ClaimableBalanceContext.title: ClaimableBalanceContext

ClawbackContext.description:
A forced withdrawal: units leave the holder's balance under the
asset's clawback authority. It is neither a delivery, a payment nor a redemption burn,
and by itself it proves no breach of any operation.

Four roles stay apart: the holder whose balance decreases is the effect's
``account`` (or its ``holder`` when it is not an account); ``issuer`` is the asset's
issuer; the authority is the issuer for a Classic operation (``operation_source``, who
submitted it, which the protocol requires to be the issuer) and the SAC admin for a
contract call, which no SAC event names (``operation_source`` None); the counterparty
is the issuer as the supply side, because clawed-back units leave circulation: it is
neither a credit to the issuer's balance nor proof of who authorized it.

``operation_type`` is what Horizon reports for the Classic operation (None on a SAC
event, which does not name it).
ClawbackContext.title: ClawbackContext

CoverageFilter.description:
One restriction applied to the export: keep only records whose ``field`` is in
``values``. Only filters on the evaluated predicate's own account, currency or fact
type can be shown to keep every record a control needs.
CoverageFilter.title: CoverageFilter

CoverageScope.description:
What the export covered beyond source, fact types and interval (on the certificate):
the accounts and currencies, and every filter applied.
CoverageScope.title: CoverageScope

DisclosedOutcomes.description: MATCH, BREAK and UNKNOWN of the original report's admitted conclusions, copied.
DisclosedOutcomes.title: DisclosedOutcomes

DisclosedOutside.description: Included operations without an admitted conclusion: not a result.
DisclosedOutside.title: DisclosedOutside

DisclosureListView.description: Views issued to the principal of this access profile, not revoked, newest first.
DisclosureListView.title: DisclosureListView

DomainEventRecord.description:
A persisted event: the payload plus record metadata the store assigned.
``tenant_seq`` is the confirmed derivation order within the tenant: not economic
order, not the order of the facts, never global.
DomainEventRecord.title: DomainEventRecord

EvaluationEntry.description: A stored evaluation, placed at the knowledge time of its snapshot.
EvaluationEntry.title: EvaluationEntry

EvaluationPublishedData.description:
``result`` is the stored aggregate of the published evaluation (precedence of
``aggregate()``): MATCH only if every mandatory control passed with coverage; BREAK if
a mandatory control failed; UNKNOWN otherwise, which is not non-payment and not a
loss. It was current at its publication (compare-and-swap); it may be stale now.
EvaluationPublishedData.title: EvaluationPublishedData

EventNotice.description:
A change of readable types since the cursor was issued (the cursor is authenticated,
so this compares with what this server issued). ``widened``: events of these types up
to ``examined_without_delivery_through`` were examined without being delivered; to
read them, start again from the beginning with ``types`` set to them.
EventNotice.title: EventNotice

EventPageView.description:
One page of the tenant's event feed, in tenant_seq order (derivation order).

``examined`` positions run from ``examined_after`` (exclusive) to
``continuation_position`` (inclusive): each was delivered or is excluded by the filter
or by permissions. ``stop_reason``: ``end_observed`` (the head of this read), a work
limit (``work_limit``: more may follow, even if the page is empty), the item or byte
limit (the next authorized event was not delivered and is not passed over), or
``start_now``. ``observed_head`` reveals the feed's volume (accepted for events:read).
EventPageView.title: EventPageView

EvidenceEntry.description: A revision epoch: evidence (or a registration) that invalidated the conclusion.
EvidenceEntry.title: EvidenceEntry

ExchangeContext.description:
DEX origin of a fill, as Horizon reports the operation and, for a Classic fill, the
trade. ``operation_source`` is a technical party: a fill is an effect on the offer
owner's account, never a payment by or to whoever submitted the operation.
ExchangeContext.title: ExchangeContext

IntegrityReportListView.description:
Registered reports of the access profile's tenant, newest registration first. Built
from registry columns: a listed report is verified only when it is read.
IntegrityReportListView.title: IntegrityReportListView

IntegrityReportSummaryView.description:
A registered report without its cases: figures with numerator, denominator and cases
key, versions and times. No member lists, raw evidence, local paths or access-profile
data (principal, scopes). Projected from the stored document; never recomputed.
IntegrityReportSummaryView.title: IntegrityReportSummaryView

MetricView.description: A count, or a ratio with both terms; never a bare percentage.
MetricView.title: MetricView

PathPaymentContext.description:
The Classic operation as Horizon reports it. Amounts are executed amounts (None
when the operation failed); declared limits (sendMax, destMin) are never used.
PathPaymentContext.title: PathPaymentContext

PositionChangePayload.description: A TA journal entry that moves the holding or the reservations of an account.
PositionChangePayload.title: PositionChangePayload

PositionPayload.description:
Holding and pending reservations of the account at a TA journal point.

``sequence`` orders the snapshot against the TA journal: it includes every entry up to
and including that sequence. Equal timestamps never order entries by themselves.
PositionPayload.title: PositionPayload

PricePayload.description: An approved, versioned price per unit (``price_ref`` names the version).
PricePayload.title: PricePayload

PriorPublication.description:
The latest publication when the epoch opened. ``current_until_reopening`` is true
only if it belonged to the epoch just closed (otherwise it was already stale).
PriorPublication.title: PriorPublication

QuarantinedRecord.description:
One quarantined input record and the ledger addresses it involves.

``addresses`` None means its parties are unknown (e.g. an undecodable record): it then
affects every operation evaluated on the certificate.

Optional, absent when None so that earlier certificates stay identical:

- ``nature``: what the evidence establishes about the record. ``clawback_identified``:
  the event or operation identifies a clawback (the protocol emits it only for one) and
  only its correspondence or origin is incomplete. ``movement_identified``: a movement
  whose kind and parties are identified (a contract or pool movement, a claimable
  balance effect with read participants) and that no current profile admits as
  evidence. ``contradictory``: the sources
  disagree on whether it was a clawback or something else. ``unresolved``: nature,
  execution, asset or participants not resolved. Absent (an earlier certificate) is
  read as ``unresolved``.
- ``chain_operation``: ``<tx_hash>:<op_index>`` of the ledger operation, when known.
- ``execution_links``: the operations whose explicit ExecutionLink names that ledger
  operation. The link makes the record relevant to those operations; its addresses
  are kept as they are, never replaced by unknown parties.
QuarantinedRecord.title: QuarantinedRecord

RedemptionCancellationPayload.description: A business cancellation of a request, distinct from retracting evidence.
RedemptionCancellationPayload.title: RedemptionCancellationPayload

RedemptionReactivationPayload.description: A business reactivation of a cancelled request (unsupported in this profile).
RedemptionReactivationPayload.title: RedemptionReactivationPayload

RedemptionRequestPayload.description:
A redemption request accepted by the TA: a fixed quantity, settled in full.

``accepted_at`` and ``payment_due_at`` are both explicit; the profile fixes how the
second follows from the first, and the engine checks it rather than trusting it.
RedemptionRequestPayload.title: RedemptionRequestPayload

SelectedEvaluation.description: The publication the selection policy picked for an operation (admitted or not).
SelectedEvaluation.title: SelectedEvaluation

SourceRecord.description: Idempotency identity of a source record: same key + revision = same statement.
SourceRecord.title: SourceRecord

SupersededCertificate.description:
A certificate a later one replaces, by id and by the sha256 of its canonical JSON
(``certificate_sha256``): two runs can produce one id with different content, and a
replacement holds only for the content it names.
SupersededCertificate.title: SupersededCertificate

TechnicalErrorsChange.description:
Controls whose stored ``reason_code`` is ``EVALUATION_ERROR`` (contract: a technical
error, always UNKNOWN). A change is reported as observed; it is never asserted to be a
correction of the earlier error.
TechnicalErrorsChange.title: TechnicalErrorsChange

TemporalView.description: What each time of a report means (report format 1.1).
TemporalView.title: TemporalView

TokenMovementPayload.description:
A movement of the target asset between two base accounts.

``from_muxed_id``/``to_muxed_id``: the sub-account id of a muxed
(M) sender or receiver, as the Classic operation names it; None when that side is not
muxed (an id of 0 is a muxed id). The balance that moves is the base account's; who holds
the sub-account is not known from the id, and an IdentityLink to the base account does
not approve it. ``memo`` is the transaction's memo when the representation read
it (the Classic payment, mapping 1.1.0 on); None means it was not read, never that the
transaction has none (that is ``memo_type: none``). All three are absent from the
serialized form when None, so earlier artifacts stay identical.
TokenMovementPayload.title: TokenMovementPayload

TransactionMemo.description:
The memo of the whole transaction, exactly as the ledger holds it.

Its scope is the transaction (``ChainCoordinates.tx_hash``), never one operation, and
it is context: it never links an observation to an operation (only an explicit
ExecutionLink does) and it never identifies a muxed sub-account. A memo id and a muxed id
that are numerically equal are different things.

``value`` by type: ``none`` none; ``text`` the exact bytes (0 to 28, not necessarily
UTF-8) in padded base64; ``id`` a canonical decimal u64; ``hash`` and ``return`` the 32
bytes in lowercase hex.
TransactionMemo.title: TransactionMemo

TransactionOutcome.description:
The whole transaction's technical result: fee (XLM stroops) and Horizon's
``result_xdr`` when it reports one. Repeated on each effect of the operation for
context; it is never apportioned nor summed per effect.
TransactionOutcome.title: TransactionOutcome

UnresolvedOrigin.description: Why a SAC movement could not be told apart from a DEX fill or another effect.
UnresolvedOrigin.title: UnresolvedOrigin

invaria__contracts__events__Provenance.description:
Where the event comes from and when the fact was recorded.

``fact_recorded_at`` is the store clock of the fact itself (epoch opened, publication
committed, report registered), not the derivation time (record ``derived_at``) and not
an economic time. ``source_payload``: ``pinned`` when the fact's transaction wrote the
references this event names (current code); ``historical`` when the outbox row predates
pinned references and those references were read back from append-only history.
invaria__contracts__events__Provenance.title: Provenance

consoleToken.description: per-process token printed at startup (or its session cookie)

info.description: Local, read-only REST served by `invaria console serve` on 127.0.0.1. Tenant, principal and scopes come from the operator's access profile, never from the request. Only GET and HEAD. Not an institutional API.
info.title: Invaria local evidence console (read-only)

404.description: NOT_FOUND: absent, or of another tenant (existence is never confirmed); for a disclosed view, also issued to another principal or revoked

422.description: VALIDATION_ERROR: invalid parameter, cursor, key or limit. EVENT_EXCEEDS_MAX_BYTES: the next authorized event does not fit max_bytes (details.required_bytes); retry larger

503.description: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE: the evidence store is unavailable (retryable)

get.summary: Epochs, snapshots and evaluations of an operation
